title: Two Values That Snuck In Twice
statement:
A list was supposed to hold each integer from 0 to n − 1 exactly once. Two different values were added a second time, so nums has length n + 2 and is in no particular order.

Return the two values that appear twice, in any order.

examples.why: n = 3. Both 0 and 2 appear twice. [2, 0] is accepted too.
n = 4, and the extra copies are a 3 and a 1.

constraints: Exactly two different values appear twice; all others appear once
hints: The values are small, from 0 to n − 1. What does that let you use instead of a general hash map?
Count occurrences in an array of size n and collect the values whose count reaches 2.
For O(1) extra space: XOR everything with 0..n−1 to get x ⊕ y, then split the numbers by one set bit of that result to separate x from y.

explain.intuition:
Each value is a valid index into an array of size n, so a counting array (or a set) finds the repeats in one pass: the moment a value is seen for the second time, it is one of the two.

A neat O(1)-space alternative uses XOR. XOR all of nums together with 0, 1, …, n − 1: every value that appears an even number of times in total cancels, and what is left is x ⊕ y. Because x ≠ y, that result has at least one 1 bit, a bit where x and y differ. XOR again, but only over numbers that have that bit set; this group isolates one of the two, and the other is (x ⊕ y) ⊕ it.
steps: Create a seen array of size n filled with false, and an empty result.
For each value v: if seen[v] is already true, add v to the result; otherwise mark it.
Return the result once it holds two values.
pitfalls: Using the sum trick alone. The sum gives x + y, but you need a second equation (sum of squares or XOR split) to recover both.
Adding a value to the result on every repeat sighting. With exactly two copies that is fine, but a counting version that checks count ≥ 2 adds it again on a third copy.
In the XOR split, choosing a bit that is 0 in x ⊕ y. Then both repeats land in the same group.

complexity.space: O(n), or O(1) with the XOR split

solutions.title: Compare every pair
solutions.idea: Two equal values at different positions mark a repeat.

solutions.title: Seen array
solutions.idea: Mark each value in a boolean array indexed by value; a second sighting is a repeat.

solutions.title: XOR split
solutions.idea: XOR of nums and 0..n−1 is x ⊕ y. One set bit of it separates x from y into two groups that XOR down to each value.

followups: Exactly one value is repeated and one value from 0..n−1 is missing. How do you find both?
The array is read-only and you have O(1) extra space, but the repeated values may appear many times. What changes?
lcTitle: The Two Sneaky Numbers of Digitville
